heroIntro: The Supreme Court of Bangladesh—comprising the High Court Division and the Appellate Division—stands as the guardian of the Constitution and the highest temple of justice in the republic. While local Magistrate Courts and District Sessions Courts adjudicate everyday civil and criminal trials, moving to the Supreme Court becomes imperative when constitutional rights are trampled by government authorities, lower courts commit jurisdictional errors, or severe criminal convictions must be appealed. Founded and led by Advocate Md. Shah Alam, an enrolled Advocate of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh, our chambers in Uttara, Dhaka and the Supreme Court Bar Association Annex provide decisive constitutional advocacy, criminal defense, and appellate representation. This guide clarifies exactly when, why, and how to approach the High Court Division.

quickAnswer.heading: ⚡ High Court Division Jurisdiction at a Glance
points: Writ Petition (Article 102 of the Constitution): Invoked when fundamental rights are breached, or statutory authorities (RAJUK, Customs, Universities, Police) act arbitrarily without alternative legal remedy.
Five Constitutional Writs: Mandamus (compelling public duty), Certiorari (quashing unlawful orders), Habeas Corpus (releasing illegal detainees), Prohibition, and Quo-Warranto.
Criminal Appeal (Section 410 Cr.P.C.): Filed before the High Court Division against convictions and sentences passed by Sessions Judges or Special Tribunals.
Criminal Revision (Section 439) & Quashment (Section 561A): Rectifying lower court miscarriages of justice and stopping baseless criminal harassment.

sections.h2: The Judicial Hierarchy: Lower Judiciary vs. High Court Division
sections.content:
In Bangladesh, original trials commence in subordinate courts—such as Assistant Judge Courts for civil suits or Magistrate/Sessions Courts for criminal charges. However, subordinate courts are bounded by strict statutory procedures and cannot question government circulars, statutory rules, or executive high-handedness.

The High Court Division of the Supreme Court exercises extraordinary constitutional writ jurisdiction, original company and admiralty jurisdiction, and comprehensive appellate and revisional powers over all subordinate courts.

sections.h2: When Do You Need a Writ Petition Under Article 102?
sections.content:
A Writ Petition under Article 102 of the Constitution of Bangladesh is your constitutional shield against state overreach. You require a writ petition when:

  • A statutory body or government agency (e.g., RAJUK, BTRC, NBR, City Corporation, Police) violates your fundamental rights guaranteed under Part III of the Constitution.
  • An administrative tribunal or licensing authority arbitrarily cancels your trade license, passport, utility connection, or tender bid without due process.
  • Government officials refuse to discharge a mandatory statutory duty that the law compels them to perform.
  • Crucial Rule: A writ is maintainable only if there is no other equally efficacious alternative legal remedy provided by ordinary statute.

sections.h2: The 5 Major Classes of Writs Explained (Mandamus, Certiorari, Habeas Corpus)
sections.content:
1. Writ of Mandamus: An order compelling a public officer, government department, or statutory corporation to perform a mandatory statutory duty they have neglected or refused to execute.
  2. Writ of Certiorari: An order quashing and declaring null and void an illegal, arbitrary, or unconstitutional order passed by an administrative body or inferior tribunal exceeding its jurisdiction.
  3. Writ of Habeas Corpus: An emergency directive commanding law enforcement to produce a person unlawfully detained in custody before the High Court and secure their immediate release.
  4. Writ of Prohibition: An order restraining a lower tribunal or authority from proceeding with a matter outside its legal jurisdiction.
  5. Writ of Quo-Warranto: Inquiring by what warrant or legal authority a person holds a public office.

sections.h2: Mandatory Prerequisite: The Demand for Justice Notice
sections.content: Except in emergency applications for Habeas Corpus, the High Court requires the petitioner to serve a formal written Demand for Justice Notice upon the respondent authorities. This statutory notice gives the government authority a reasonable timeframe (typically 7 to 15 days) to rectify the illegality before invoking constitutional jurisdiction.

sections.h2: Criminal Appeals under Section 410 Cr.P.C.: Overturning Lower Court Convictions
sections.content:
When an individual is convicted and sentenced by a Court of Sessions Judge, Additional Sessions Judge, or Special Tribunal (such as Anti-Corruption Commission or Cyber Tribunal):

  • An appeal lies directly to the High Court Division under Section 410 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
  • The High Court has the power to admit the appeal, suspend the sentence, call for the lower court records (LCR), and grant bail to the convict pending disposal of the appeal.
  • Upon hearing the complete Paper Book, the High Court Bench can set aside the conviction and acquit the appellant.

sections.h2: Section 561A Cr.P.C.: Quashing False Criminal Cases in the High Court
sections.content: Where a criminal proceeding in a lower court is manifestly baseless, politically motivated, or used to enforce a civil contract, the High Court Division exercises inherent power under Section 561A Cr.P.C. to prevent abuse of the process of the court and secure the ends of justice by quashing the proceedings completely.

faqs.question: Can anyone file a Writ Petition directly in the Supreme Court?
faqs.answer: Any aggrieved citizen whose fundamental rights are violated, or who suffers from an arbitrary government order without alternative legal recourse, can file a Writ Petition through an enrolled Advocate of the Supreme Court.

faqs.question: What is an interim stay order (Stay) in a Writ Petition?
faqs.answer: Upon admitting a writ petition, the High Court Division frequently issues an ad-interim stay order or injunction halting the execution of the disputed government order (e.g., stopping auction, demolition, or disciplinary action) until final judgment.

faqs.question: How long does a Criminal Appeal take in the High Court?
faqs.answer: While admission and interim bail can be secured within 1–2 weeks, final hearing depends on the preparation of the official Paper Book containing complete evidence from the lower court.
